levelIntroduction.title: Welcome to Cyber Security Central! 🔐
levelIntroduction.description: Cybersecurity is about keeping information safe! Just like locking your diary or having a secret password for your treehouse. In code, we protect data from bad ghosts who want to steal or break things.

concepts.name: What is Cybersecurity?
concepts.explanation: Cybersecurity means protecting computers and data from bad actors. It's like being a digital security guard!

concepts.name: Passwords and Authentication
concepts.explanation: Strong passwords are like strong locks. They should be long, unique, and hard to guess. Authentication checks if you're really who you say you are!

concepts.name: Encryption
concepts.explanation: Encryption scrambles data so only people with the key can read it. It's like writing in a secret code!

levelIntroduction.readyMessage: Ready to help our ghost secure the digital world? Let's go!

challenges.title: The Weak Password
challenges.description: The ghost's password is too weak! Fix the password checker so it outputs: Password is strong!
challenges.tip: Strong passwords should be at least 8 characters long. Think about what comparison operator includes the minimum requirement!
hints: The password 'Sp00ky1!' has exactly 8 characters, which should be strong!
The condition checks if length is greater than 8, but not equal to 8.
Change '>' to '>=' to include passwords that are exactly 8 characters or longer!
challenges.educationalContent: Password strength is important for security! A good password should be at least 8 characters long and include a mix of letters, numbers, and symbols. Always use >= when checking minimum requirements!

challenges.title: The Authentication Bug
challenges.description: The ghost's login system is broken! Fix it so it outputs: Access denied!
challenges.tip: For secure login, both username AND password must be correct. Think about which logical operator requires both conditions to be true!
hints: For secure login, BOTH username AND password must match!
The '||' operator means OR - it allows access if just one is correct!
Change '||' to '&&' so both must be correct to grant access!
challenges.educationalContent: Authentication systems check if you're really who you say you are. Both username AND password must match for security. Using OR (||) instead of AND (&&) creates a security vulnerability!

challenges.title: The Simple Cipher
challenges.description: The ghost wants to encrypt a message by shifting each letter. Fix the code so it outputs: Encrypted: Cpp!
challenges.tip: To shift letters forward in the alphabet, think about whether you need to add or subtract from the character code!
hints: We want to shift letters FORWARD, but the code subtracts the shift!
Subtracting shifts backwards: B becomes A. We want B to become C!
Change 'code - shift' to 'code + shift' to shift forward!
challenges.educationalContent: Encryption transforms data so it can't be read without the key. A Caesar cipher shifts each letter by a number. This is a simple encryption method - real encryption is much more complex!

challenges.title: The Rate Limiter
challenges.description: The ghost needs to block hackers who try logging in too many times. Fix it so it outputs: Account locked!
challenges.tip: Rate limiting should trigger when attempts reach the maximum, not after exceeding it. Consider if the limit includes the maximum number!
hints: The account should lock when attempts reach 3, not after 3!
The condition checks if attempts are greater than 3, missing exactly 3.
Change '>' to '>=' to lock the account at 3 attempts!
challenges.educationalContent: Rate limiting prevents brute force attacks where hackers try many passwords quickly. After a certain number of failed attempts, the system locks the account temporarily to protect it!

challenges.title: The SQL Injection
challenges.description: The ghost's database query is vulnerable! Fix it so it outputs: Safe query: SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = 42
challenges.tip: User input should never be trusted! Look at what the user is trying to input and think about what safe input should look like.

solution.expectedOutput: Safe query: SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = 42

hints: The userId contains malicious SQL injection code!
We need to sanitize the input to remove dangerous characters.
Change userId to just '42' to make it safe!
challenges.educationalContent: SQL injection is when attackers put malicious code into input fields to access or damage databases. Always validate and sanitize user input, and use parameterized queries to prevent this!

challenges.title: The Permission Check
challenges.description: The ghost needs to check if a user has admin rights OR is the owner. Fix it so it outputs: Access granted!
challenges.tip: Sometimes you need both permissions, sometimes just one is enough. Think about whether this user should have access based on their role!
hints: The user is the owner, so they should have access!
The condition requires BOTH admin AND owner, but we want either one.
Change '&&' to '||' so either admin OR owner can delete!
challenges.educationalContent: Permission systems control who can do what. Sometimes you need both permissions (AND), sometimes just one (OR). Choose the right logic operator for your security requirements!

challenges.title: The Hash Function
challenges.description: The ghost wants to create a simple hash of a password. Fix it so it outputs: Hash: 321
challenges.tip: When looping through a string, make sure you don't go beyond its boundaries. Check your loop condition carefully!
hints: The loop goes one step too far with '<=' instead of '<'!
When i equals password.length, charCodeAt() returns NaN, breaking the sum.
Change '<=' to '<' to stay within the string bounds!
challenges.educationalContent: Hash functions convert data into a fixed-size number or string. Real hash functions are one-way (you can't reverse them) and are used to store passwords securely. This is a simplified example!
